exposure: patient-level characteristics (race/ethnicity, income, age, insurance type)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 245,383 low-risk women who underwent delivery in Maryland, Florida, and Wisconsin between 2017 and 2020, with a mean age of approximately 26.9 years.
finding: The study found an increasing rate of cesarean sections among low-risk women between 2017 and 2020, with higher rates associated with being Hispanic or Black, having private insurance, and delivering in a for-profit hospital.
mod_finding: The study identified an increasing rate of cesarean section among low-risk women and linked higher cesarean section utilization to specific demographic (Hispanic or Black), socioeconomic (private insurance), and hospital characteristics (for-profit hospital).
